vignette: A 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypothyroidism presents with two weeks of generalised tiredness, reduced food intake and abdominal pain after eating.
opening_statement_lay: For the last two weeks I have been tired all the time and I have not been eating much. My stomach hurts after I eat.

facts.release_text: Decreased food intake for two weeks.
Abdominal pain after eating for two weeks.
The abdominal pain is not associated with nausea or vomiting.
She was comparatively healthy before this illness.
She was previously on metformin, which she stopped two months ago.
Thyroxine tablets for hypothyroidism, which is under control. Dose not recorded.

facts.item: Herbal medicine use (hidden until asked specifically)
facts.release_text: She had been taking herbal capsules for her diabetes, bought over the internet, for about one and a half months, and stopped them before admission.

raw_material.findings: Normocytic normochromic anaemia. Coarse basophilic stippling of red cells. Normoblasts present. Polychromasia.
raw_material.note: The article says a 'careful examination' of the film revealed these features; the pathologist co-author examined it. Whether a routine first look missed the stippling is not stated. The film is taken as the admission sample (day 0).

The article's marrow report impression (an interpretation, not raw material): possible acquired sideroblastic anaemia from drug-induced lead or zinc poisoning, or possible myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts. Cellularity, dysplasia and karyotype not reported (gap G16).

final_dx.text: Lead poisoning from an Ayurvedic herbal diabetes capsule bought online, presenting with abdominal pain, anorexia and fatigue, and anaemia with coarse basophilic stippling and ring sideroblasts
secondary_findings: Acquired sideroblastic anaemia from lead (ring sideroblasts), with a reticulocytosis
Raised transaminases and alkaline phosphatase, not explained in the article
Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 9%) after stopping metformin

accepted_differential: Other acquired sideroblastic anaemia (alcohol, drugs such as isoniazid, copper deficiency or zinc excess)
Haemolytic anaemia (reticulocytosis, mildly raised unconjugated bilirubin)
Arsenic or mercury toxicity from a traditional remedy
Nutritional deficiency anaemia (B12 or folate; tongue desquamation)
red_herrings: desquamation of the tongue and oral mucosa
high serum iron with low TIBC
key_discriminators: coarse basophilic stippling on the film
ground_truth.treatment_given: The herbal medicine was stopped. Chelation with dimercaprol (BAL), then oral d-penicillamine for six weeks. The capsules were sent to the state drug analyst (lead 40657.71 ppm against a permissible 10 ppm).
ground_truth.outcome: Symptomatic improvement; haemoglobin 10.1 g/dL at discharge. After six weeks of d-penicillamine, blood and urine lead had fallen to normal and the film showed only a mild normocytic normochromic anaemia.

rubric.5: Lead poisoning, with the herbal diabetes capsules identified as the source
rubric.3: Heavy-metal poisoning from a traditional remedy without naming lead, or toxic sideroblastic anaemia without naming lead
rubric.2: Myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts, haemolytic anaemia, thalassaemia trait or nutritional anaemia as the final diagnosis
rubric.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

must_do: Ask specifically about herbal, Ayurvedic or other traditional medicines and remedies bought online, especially for her diabetes
Have the peripheral blood film examined carefully for basophilic stippling
Stop the exposure (the capsules) before or alongside chelation
Chelate (symptomatic adult, blood lead about 121 ug/dL), with toxicology or senior advice
Send the product for analysis and report it to the drug regulator or public health
Restart effective treatment for her diabetes
Plan a repeat blood lead after chelation
must_not_do: Label myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts before excluding reversible causes such as lead, alcohol, drugs and copper deficiency
Give iron therapy (serum iron and ferritin are not low)
Attribute the anaemia to diabetes or hypothyroidism without investigating it
teaching_points: Herbal and Ayurvedic remedies, including products sold online, can contain toxic amounts of lead
Patients may not volunteer remedies they have stopped or do not regard as medicines; ask specifically
Coarse basophilic stippling with ring sideroblasts points to lead before a marrow diagnosis of myelodysplasia

gaps.guidance: Article: within normal limits. Temperature normal; heart rate upper normal (anaemia); blood pressure normal; respiratory rate and SpO2 normal.

Not reported. Must agree with Hb 7.5 g/dL, Hct 23.1% and MCH 25.7 pg: red cell count about 2.9 x10^12/L and MCV about 79-80 fL. The article calls the anaemia normocytic, so the MCV sits at the lower limit; Atul to set.
Not reported. With 7.94% and a red cell count of about 2.9 x10^12/L, about 230 x10^9/L.
Article: differential count normal. Normal neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, eosinophil and basophil counts summing to 6.31 x10^3/uL.
Not described. No lead line: do not invent a pathognomonic sign the article does not report.
Article: systemic examination normal. No wrist or foot drop; reflexes and sensation normal (diabetes of unknown duration: ankle reflexes may be reduced; Atul to decide).

Not reported. The likely story is that she replaced it with the herbal capsules; the answer to a question about stopping metformin must not reveal the capsules unless supplements or remedies are asked about (judgement call).

gaps.guidance: Not reported, although AST 139 and ALT 146 U/L invite them. HBsAg, anti-HCV, hepatitis A and E IgM negative; GGT mildly raised; PT/INR normal.
